messages:
emma: follow-up from RFC: we need a clear contract for gateway cancel vs client reconnect semantics for streaming responses. two user stories: 1) low-latency interactive clients that expect immediate connection close on cancel, 2) long-running streams that want resumability on flaky mobile networks. proposing an opt-in header `Accept-Resume: yes` + server-side tenant toggle.

raj: agree on opt-in. question: how do we handle partial-server-side work? e.g., model produced tokens but we can't flush because of in-flight IO. do we emit a resume token immediately or wait to produce trailer metadata?

taylor: emit a resume token as soon as we know the KV-cache checkpoint and offset. it means we might emit a lightweight trailer early and let the client close. heavy-weight checkpointing (e.g., full activation snapshots) should be async and stored behind resume token reference.

noah: concerns: if we hand out resume tokens, we need a revocation/TTL policy and a way to cleanup cached resume state to avoid unbounded memory growth. propose default TTL 10m and per-tenant override. also cap resumable entries per-tenant to N (e.g., 100).

emma: good point. also need to design token contents. minimum: tenant_id, model_id, model_revision, token_offset, kv_cache_digest, issued_at, nonce. sign with HMAC using tenant key. include a short opaque ref to server-side state when we can't serialize full checkpoint.

raj: operationally we should expose metrics: resume_token_issued, resume_success, resume_mismatch (when resumed state doesn't align). and surface in console so customers can opt-in after seeing error rates.

taylor: race condition: client cancels then rapidly reconnects; server may still be finalizing checkpoint. resume flow should accept 'in-progress' state: return HTTP 202 Accept with resume-accepted header allowing client to poll or reconnect with same token. avoid blocking client.

noah: retries vs fallbacks: do we ever auto-fallback to smaller model on cancel/resume? risky for determinism. suggest gateway only auto-fallback for read-only completions when tenant enabled and request is marked as tolerant. otherwise require client-driven retry.

emma: agreed. add a request header `X-Resume-Tolerance: best-effort` if client allows fallback and potential content drift. document consequences to billing and eval reproducibility.

infra-bot: created issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rfcs/issues/472 (resume-token-lifecycle)

emma: action items:
- write resume-token spec + HMAC example (go/python) @raj
- define server-side state lifecycle & TTL defaults @noah
- add metrics & console UX wires @taylor
- update API docs with Accept-Resume and X-Resume-Tolerance semantics @emma

raj: small note: make sure we include a client-friendly error code when resume fails (4xx vs 5xx) so SDKs can implement clear retry logic.

noah: will prototype a GC worker for expired resume entries and add tenant quota enforcement.

emma: ok wrapping up. we'll merge RFC v2 after we have the HMAC examples and the TTL proposal. thanks all!
thread_summary: Design follow-up for resumable streaming: opt-in Accept-Resume header, resume-token contents and HMAC signing, TTL and per-tenant quotas, async checkpointing with 202 polling, metrics and console visibility, and opt-in auto-fallback controlled by X-Resume-Tolerance.
